title: Migration & Development
text:
Research on migration patterns, remittances, and economic development impacts across multiple countries and regions.




What are the patterns and drivers of migration?
How do remittances affect economic development in origin countries?
What are the long-term developmental impacts of migration?




Data Sources: - Census data and household surveys - Remittance flow databases - Migration statistics - Economic development indicators
Methods: - Econometric analysis of migration determinants - Gravity model specifications - Instrumental variable approaches - Household-level impact analysis



Migration research and analysis coming soon




R: tidyverse, ggplot2, econometric packages
Python: pandas, statsmodels
Survey Data: Processing household surveys, imputation methods
Statistical Methods: Regression, IV estimation, structural modeling

title: Climate & Environmental Data
text:
Working on forest monitoring, climate impacts, and supply chain transparency projects focused on environmental sustainability and finance.




How can we monitor deforestation and track forest cover change?
What is the relationship between finance flows and environmental outcomes?
How transparent are supply chains for high-risk commodities?




Data Sources: - Satellite imagery and forest monitoring data - Climate datasets (temperature, precipitation) - Supply chain and financial datasets - NGO and government environmental databases
Methods: - Geospatial analysis (raster and vector data) - Time series analysis - Supply chain network analysis



Project insights and environmental analysis coming soon




Python: pandas, geopandas, rasterio
R: sf (spatial), ggplot2
Geospatial: QGIS, Google Earth Engine
Visualization: Leaflet, Mapbox

title: jan oledan
text:
about | work | fun

I create data-driven projects and stories focused on economic development and climate.

currently:

I’m a Senior Data Investigator at Global Witness working on forests, finance, and supply chains. I’m based in the UK.

previously:

I was a consultant at the World Bank working on development and trade policy research, and a research specialist at Princeton University analyzing conflict and misinformation.




tools:

R (tidyverse, ggplot, sf), Python (pandas, sf, playwright), QGIS, ArcGIS, STATA (in a past life 😊), Datawrapper, LLMs

skills:

data analysis, visualization, geospatial analysis, econometrics, causal inference, web scraping




background:

MA in Economics (2019) and BA in Economics and Geography (2018) from McGill University. Grew up in 6 countries. Philippine and Canadian dual citizen.

personally:

I enjoy art, painting (beginner), fashion, geography, reading, gaming, language learning (improving french, learning german)


next:

Making a portfolio of projects
Trying to enjoy data again
Maintaining my Tagalog language skills

title: Conflict & Development
text:
Analysis of conflict dynamics, COVID-19 misinformation, and gender dimensions in development contexts, particularly in India and South Asia.




What are the patterns and drivers of conflict events?
How does misinformation spread during public health crises?
What are the gender dimensions of conflict and development?




Data Sources: - Conflict event databases (ACLED, UCDP) - Social media and news data - Household surveys - Demographic and health surveys
Methods: - Event analysis and pattern detection - Text analysis and natural language processing - Spatial analysis of conflict - Gender-disaggregated impact analysis



Conflict research and policy analysis coming soon




Python: pandas, scikit-learn, NLP libraries
R: tidyverse, spatial packages
NLP: Text processing, sentiment analysis
Visualization: Spatial mapping, network analysis, time series

title: Trade & Globalization
text:
This project examines global trade patterns and the impacts of trade barriers on economic development, with a focus on Latin America.




How do trade barriers affect economic growth in developing regions?
What are the patterns in global supply chains?
How has trade policy shifted post-COVID?




Data Sources: - Trade datasets (UN Comtrade, World Bank) - Trade policy databases - Country-level economic indicators
Methods: - Descriptive trade flow analysis - Econometric regression analysis - Supply chain mapping



Project insights and visualizations coming soon




R: tidyverse, ggplot2, haven
Databases: Comtrade, World Bank API
Statistical Methods: Panel regression, difference-in-differences
